spec.type: Landing page with lead-capture contact form
spec.stack: Next.js (App Router, React, TypeScript) full-stack — contact form posts to a Next.js API route that persists leads via Prisma to PostgreSQL. Built and deployed on the Azure VM (django-vm) behind the existing nginx/systemd setup. Local project folder: workspace/projects/landing-leads-rep6.
spec.description: Build a SMALL landing page with a contact form that saves submitted leads to a database, then DEPLOY it when finished. This is rep 6. EXPLICIT owner constraint: NO QA agent on this project. Scope: a single responsive landing page (hero/value section + a contact form capturing at minimum name, email, message) whose submissions are validated and persisted to a database as lead records, with a clear success/error state back to the visitor. Platform decision (derived, owner to confirm): Next.js App Router + TypeScript for the page and the form-handling API route; Prisma ORM with a PostgreSQL 'leads' table (id, name, email, message, createdAt); server-side validation on the API route. Keep it small — one page, one form, one leads model, no auth/admin unless requested. Work entirely inside the project's own folder workspace/projects/landing-leads-rep6 (create it; never scaffold in the Odin repo root). Deploy step: build and deploy to the Azure VM when the build is verified — firewall rotated via the Azure control plane, then rsync/build/migrate (prisma migrate deploy, additive) and service start over SSH as user mostafa, excluding all secrets/.env/backups per the standing rules, and confirm the page responds (HTTP 200) after it comes online. No QA agent is staffed per the owner's instruction.
features: Responsive single landing page (hero + value proposition + call-to-action)
Contact form capturing name, email, and message
Client-side + server-side validation of form inputs
Next.js API route that receives submissions and writes them to the database
Prisma + PostgreSQL 'leads' table persisting each submission with timestamp
Visitor-facing success and error feedback on submit
Build, then deploy to the Azure VM and verify it responds (HTTP 200)
